newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares creep up in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares creep up in light trade.

text.p: Lithuanian shares crept up on Thursday but trade remained light as investors waited for the results from a spate of shareholders' meetings, dealers said.
"Things are going to stay quiet until next week, when investors digest the results of the meetings," one dealer said.
The Litin A index climbed 16.23 points to 2,638.14 and the Litin G index rose 0.38 points to 2,290.20.
Overall central market turnover was just under one million litas.
Big gainers included the Lithuania Sea Shipping Company, which regained ground lost on Wednesday, rising to 8.90 litas from 8.23 litas in trade of over 99,000 litas.
Oil refinery Maizeikiu Nafta also rose, advancing to 12.01 litas from 11.11 litas in trade worth 52,600 litas.
The company, which is 90 percent state-owned, said on Wednesday that it planned to implement a $100 million reconstruction plan in the second half of this year.
It also reported that its 1996 losses were 17.9 million litas versus 32.9 million litas the previous year.
Dealers said that Mazeikiu's investors were looking at the long-term prospects for the company and its share price.
Lithuania Gas edged down to 2.30 litas from 2.32 litas in trade of 120,000 litas.
Block trades reached over 500,000 litas and volume on the secondary T-bill market picked up, turning over almost five million litas.
